summary: AI observability has become a critical discipline as LLM applications move into production, with the market growing to an estimated $2.69 billion in 2026 and projected to reach $9.26 billion by 2030 at a 36.2% CAGR. Without proper monitoring, teams fly blind on latency spikes, cost overruns, and quality degradation across millions of model calls. Gartner predicts that by 2028, LLM observability investments will account for 50% of all GenAI deployments, up from just 15% in early 2026.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, chain execution steps, prompt inputs/outputs, latency, token usage, and errors across LangChain and LangGraph applications
features: Deep LangChain and LangGraph native integration
Rich trace debugging with full chain visualization
Dataset creation and prompt versioning
Human feedback annotation and evaluation runs
Per-trace cost and token breakdown
Team collaboration and project organization
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39/seat/month with overage around $2.50 per thousand traces; Enterprise custom pricing
tools.best_for: Teams already using LangChain or LangGraph who need rich debugging capabilities and are willing to pay a premium for deep framework integration

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests, token consumption, cost per request, latency, error rates, and user-level usage across all major model providers via a proxy gateway
features: One-line proxy setup with 2-minute integration time
Best-in-class cost visibility, optimization, and enforcement
Request caching to reduce redundant API spend
Rate limiting and spend controls per user or team
Custom properties and metadata tagging on requests
SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA compliance on Team tier
Open-source and self-hostable
tools.pricing: Free Hobby tier at 10K requests/month; Pro at $79/month (unlimited seats, usage-based beyond included volume); Team at $799/month (adds compliance); Enterprise custom with SAML SSO and on-prem options
tools.best_for: Teams that want the simplest possible setup with the best cost tracking and enforcement — ideal for startups and cost-conscious teams monitoring spend across multiple model providers

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B) Weave
tools.monitors: LLM traces, model inputs/outputs, evaluation runs, experiment metrics, dataset versions, and full ML training and fine-tuning pipelines
features: Unified platform for training, fine-tuning, and inference monitoring
Weave module for LLM tracing and evaluation
Experiment tracking with artifact versioning
Collaborative dashboards for cross-functional teams
Prompt management and evaluation pipelines
Integration with major ML frameworks and model providers
tools.pricing: Free tier available for individuals; Teams plan at $50/user/month; Enterprise custom pricing; usage-based compute charges may apply
tools.best_for: ML-heavy teams that train or fine-tune models in addition to running inference, needing a single platform that bridges research experimentation and production LLM monitoring

tools.name: Arize AI (Arize Phoenix)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, embeddings, retrieval quality in RAG pipelines, model drift, hallucination signals, and long-standing ML model performance metrics
features: Extends proven ML monitoring capabilities into the LLM era
Phoenix open-source library for local and self-hosted tracing
RAG retrieval quality and relevance scoring
Embedding drift and cluster analysis
Online evaluation integrations with 50+ metrics
Span-level trace inspection for agents and chains
Integration with OpenTelemetry standards
tools.pricing: Phoenix is fully open-source and free to self-host; Arize managed platform offers a free Developer tier; Growth and Enterprise tiers are custom-priced based on data volume
tools.best_for: Teams with existing ML models in production who are adding LLM capabilities and need unified observability across both traditional ML and generative AI workloads, especially RAG pipelines

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompt versions, token usage, cost per trace, latency, user sessions, and evaluation scores across any model provider or framework
features: Open-source with active community and self-hosting option
Detailed trace and span visualization for complex chains and agents
Prompt management with versioning and A/B testing
Native evaluation integrations and human annotation workflows
SDKs for Python, TypeScript, and OpenAI-compatible wrappers
Free Cloud tier for smaller teams and projects
tools.pricing: Cloud free tier for under 50K requests/month; paid Cloud tiers start around $20-30/month for higher volumes; Self-hosted free with approximately $30/month infrastructure cost and 2 hours/month maintenance
tools.best_for: Open-source-first teams and developers who want full data control via self-hosting, strong prompt versioning workflows, and a cost-effective entry point without vendor lock-in

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM API calls, token counts, latency, and model parameters using OpenTelemetry-native instrumentation across any model provider or orchestration framework
features: OpenTelemetry-native — exports to any existing OTel-compatible backend
Auto-instrumentation for OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, LangChain, and more
No vendor lock-in — works with Datadog, Grafana, Jaeger, or any collector
Lightweight SDK with minimal code changes required
Span attributes follow emerging semantic conventions for LLMs
Open-source under Apache 2.0 license
tools.pricing: Fully open-source and free; costs depend only on your chosen OTel backend or observability platform
tools.best_for: Engineering teams with an existing OpenTelemetry observability stack who want to add LLM monitoring without adopting a new vendor, keeping all telemetry in one place

tools.name: Confident AI
tools.monitors: LLM outputs, trace quality scores, evaluation metrics, hallucination signals, and dataset curation with real-time alerting across production deployments
features: Built around DeepEval with 50+ research-backed evaluation metrics
Every production trace automatically scored at the observability layer
Quality-aware alerting via PagerDuty, Slack, and Microsoft Teams
Automatic dataset curation from flagged production traces
Cross-functional workflows accessible to PMs, QA, and domain experts
Integrates evaluation directly into CI/CD pipelines
tools.pricing: Tiered pricing following a consumption-based model; free tier available; Pro and Enterprise pricing custom based on trace volume and team size
tools.best_for: Teams for whom output quality and safety are the primary concern — those who need evaluation to be the core of their observability strategy rather than an afterthought

tools.name: Braintrust
tools.monitors: LLM traces, evaluation scores, experiment results, prompt performance, and dataset quality in a unified platform spanning the full development and production lifecycle
features: Only platform combining monitoring, evaluation, and experimentation in a single system
Generous Starter tier with 1 million spans/month free
Prompt playground with side-by-side model comparison
Dataset management and golden set curation from production traces
Real-time production scoring and regression detection
Used by AI teams at Notion, Vercel, and Instacart
tools.pricing: Starter tier free at 1 million spans/month; Pro at $249/month; Enterprise custom pricing
tools.best_for: AI-native product teams that need a single system for iterating on prompts, running evaluations, and monitoring production quality without stitching together multiple tools

cost_tips: Implement request-level caching for repeated or semantically similar prompts — tools like Helicone offer built-in caching that can eliminate redundant API calls and reduce spend by 20-40% for use cases with repetitive queries such as FAQs or code assistants

Right-size your model selection by routing requests based on complexity — use smaller, cheaper models like GPT-4o-mini or Claude Haiku for simple classification or extraction tasks, and reserve frontier models for genuinely complex reasoning, which can cut per-request costs by 10x or more

Set hard spend controls and rate limits per user, team, or feature using gateway tools like Helicone, and configure alerting thresholds so cost anomalies trigger Slack or PagerDuty notifications before they become runaway bills

Audit and optimize prompt token counts regularly — bloated system prompts, redundant context, and over-fetched RAG chunks are among the top sources of wasted token spend; trimming prompt length by 30% on high-volume endpoints can compound into significant monthly savings at scale
